additional_concerns: The source assigns continuing ultimate responsibility but supplies no complete test for effective retention or discharge through supervision. Governance, practical authority and conduct are possible evidence, not source-established sufficient conditions.

Retained accountability, adequate supervision and satisfactory outcomes must remain distinct. Neither an operational failure alone nor formally retained authority alone conclusively answers the typed question.

The record-keeping and operational-compatibility duty in unit 2 is separate from retention of responsibility. Section 6.11C concerns valuation outsourcing and does not automatically supply a general Product Provider supervision test.

Paragraph 14 leaves confirmation unconditioned on an SFC request and expressly conditions demonstration on a request. Footnote 5 specifies minimum substantive content but repeats confirmation and demonstration without the trigger; whether this independently broadens demonstration remains unresolved. The SFC-satisfaction wording directly attaches to demonstration, while its application to confirmation is less explicit.

No SFC request does not extinguish continuing responsibility, record-keeping duties or confirmation. Paragraphs 15 and 16 separately condition obtaining third-party audit or verification and a satisfactory legal opinion on an SFC request.

Footnote 5 references paragraphs 10–13, whose complete contents are not supplied. Full assessment of its minimum compliance content requires the remaining provisions. No external dependency identifiers are supplied.
No executable expressions or actual arrangement facts are supplied. This review establishes neither executable fidelity nor satisfaction of the Product Provider requirement.
